transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Oh, hello. Thank you for seeing me, doctor. I really appreciate you taking the time. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place for this, and I certainly don't want to be a bother. 

I guess I'm here because... well, I've been under a lot of stress at my job. I'm a computer support specialist, so I'm usually a very logical, facts-based person, you know? But for over a year now, I've just been trying to get someone to take my situation seriously. 

They implemented this new ticket rotation at work, along with these constant security audits, and... well, I know how it might sound, but I really believe they're being used to build a paper trail against me. I've tried bringing it up politely, and management just keeps showing me system logs and saying it's just standard company policy. But... I just know what I'm seeing. I don't want to cause any trouble at the office, I really don't, but I just needed someone to listen to me. I hope that makes sense? Is it alright that I came in to talk about this?
Do you feel certain that your workplace is deliberately building a case against you?

Well... yes, I do. I know I probably sound a bit, um, unreasonable saying it out loud like that. I really don't want to come across as a difficult employee, I promise I'm usually very easygoing. 

But... yes. Like I was just saying, it's been over a year of this, and I just can't get anyone there to take it seriously. Every time I try to talk about it, management just points to the system logs and tells me the security audits and ticket rotations are just standard policy. But I've been in this field a long time, and... well, I know a paper trail when I see one. I'm certain that's what it is, even if they won't admit it to me. 

I hope you don't think I'm just being paranoid or making a fuss over nothing? I really don't want to waste your time, I just... I know what I'm seeing. Am I explaining that okay?
Have you been hearing voices or sounds that other people don't seem to hear?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I've never heard voices or anything... I hope I didn't give you the impression that I was, um, losing my grip on reality or anything like that. I know the situation at work sounds a bit intense, but I'm completely healthy in that regard. 

My hearing is perfectly fine, just the usual office noise, you know? Phones ringing, keyboards clacking... nothing unusual. I would definitely tell you if I was experiencing something like that, I promise. I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so you can help me. Is that what you were asking? I hope I answered that clearly enough.
Do you ever feel that other people can read your thoughts?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I don't think anyone can read my thoughts. I mean, I know I've been talking about the security audits and the paper trail, but I'm a very rational person, really. I know that mind-reading isn't real. 

I just... I look at the data, the logs, the way the tickets are being routed... it's all right there on the screen. It's not about anyone being in my head, it's just about what they're doing on the network. I hope you don't think I'm the sort of person who believes in, well, science fiction things like that. I want to assure you I'm very grounded in reality. Did I answer that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Aside from what you believe is happening at work, do you have any other strong beliefs that people are trying to harm, monitor, or target you?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. It's really just the situation at the office. I mean, outside of work, my life is very quiet, very normal. I have a few friends I play golf with, I go to the grocery store... nobody is following me or monitoring me in my personal life. 

I know it probably sounds like I'm very wrapped up in this work thing, and I really hope I'm not coming across as, you know, overly suspicious in general. I'm actually a very trusting person! It's just that the evidence at the office is so specific, with the logs and the tickets. But outside of that? No, I feel perfectly safe and comfortable in my day-to-day life. I don't want you to think I'm seeing shadows around every corner or anything like that. 

Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you a complete picture, so you know I'm still very much... well, grounded, everywhere else. Is that helpful?
Have you been feeling depressed معظم days lately?

Oh, depressed? No, no, definitely not. I mean, everyone gets a little tired or stressed sometimes, especially with all the network security issues I've been dealing with at the office, but... no, I wouldn't use the word depressed at all. 

I try to keep a very positive outlook on life, really. I still enjoy my weekends, I get out and do things, play a little golf... I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself or falling apart emotionally. I'm actually a pretty upbeat guy! 

I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm doing well and giving you the right answers so we can get everything sorted out. Does that make sense?
If your managers showed you clear proof that the ticket rotation and audits were standard for everyone, would you accept that, or would you still believe they were building a case against you?

Well, um... I see what you're asking. And I really, really try to be open-minded, I do. I want to be a team player. But... well, it's been over a year now that I've been trying to get someone, anyone, to take this seriously. 

Management, they... they do show me logs. They pull up the screens and they tell me, "Look, it's just policy, it's standard." And I nod, and I listen respectfully, because I don't want to be difficult. But... the way the tickets are routed, the specific timing of the security audits... it just doesn't add up to standard policy. It really feels like they are building a paper trail specifically against me. 

I know that probably sounds a bit stubborn, and I'm really sorry if it does. I don't want to seem like I'm ignoring what they say or being insubordinate. It's just... I've been doing this job a long time, and I know how these systems work. The proof they show me just... it doesn't explain the whole picture. 

I hope you can understand why I'm having such a hard time just accepting it. I'm not trying to be a problem employee, I promise. I just want to protect myself. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as too unreasonable...
Has this situation at work caused your job performance to get worse?

Well... I wouldn't say my performance has gotten *worse*, exactly. I mean, I'm still doing my job, and I'm very dedicated to it! I'm still coming in on time, still working hard. 

But, I suppose... well, I've had to make some adjustments, just to be safe. I've started, um, avoiding a few of the bigger network projects lately. Just because I know they'll use those to scrutinize me more closely. And I've been writing much longer, very detailed notes in my support tickets—just to make sure everything is documented perfectly on my end, so they can't twist anything around. 

I guess... I guess maybe that has slowed things down a little bit. And, well, some of the team meetings have gotten a tiny bit tense because of it. It's taking a little longer to collaborate with the others. But I'm only doing it to protect myself, you know? I really don't want to be a bottleneck for the team, and I feel awful if it seems like I'm not pulling my weight. 

Do you think that sounds like I'm letting my work slip? I really try my best to keep everything running smoothly, I just have to be so careful right now. I hope that's understandable?
Before this problem at your current job began, did you generally tend to distrust other people’s motives?

Oh, no, no. Definitely not. I've always been a very... well, a very trusting person, I think. Before all this started at the office, I got along great with everyone. I never really second-guessed what people meant or thought they had hidden agendas. 

I mean, sure, you meet a difficult person here or there in life, but generally? No, I always took people at their word. I really pride myself on being easy to work with and seeing the best in folks. I wouldn't want you to think I'm some sort of naturally suspicious or cynical guy, because I'm really, really not. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of who I am, and that I'm answering your questions properly. Does that make sense?
Have you become less interested in seeing friends or doing things you usually enjoy?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I've lost interest, exactly. I still really like all my usual hobbies, and I still care about my friends very much! I'm definitely not depressed or anything like that, if that's what you're asking. 

I guess... well, lately, I haven't been going out quite as much on the weekends. But that's just because I've been so tired from, you know, having to be so vigilant at work all week. It takes a lot out of you, making sure all those logs and tickets are documented perfectly. So by Saturday, I just... I usually just want to stay in and rest. 

And, um, I haven't seen the guys for our regular golf game in a few weeks, but that's really just scheduling stuff! You know how busy everyone gets. I still enjoy it, I just haven't had the energy to get out there. 

Is it okay that I'm taking a little time for myself right now? I just feel like I need to recharge so I can handle the work week. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a hermit or something... I really am a very social person usually!
Have other people told you that you seem emotionally flat or less expressive than you used to be?

No, no one has said anything like that to me. I don't think I've changed how I express myself at all! I mean, I still smile, I still laugh at jokes when I hear them... I try to be very polite and warm with everyone I interact with. 

I'd hate to think I was coming across as cold or, um, robotic to people. That's really not me. Even with all the stress at work, I always try to keep a pleasant demeanor. If anything, I'm just a little quieter right now because I'm thinking so much about how to handle the office situation, but I definitely wouldn't say I'm flat. 

I really try to make sure people feel comfortable around me. Do I seem flat to you? I hope I'm being expressive enough in our conversation... I just want to make sure I'm giving you a good sense of who I am.
Have other people told you that your speech or thinking seems disorganized or hard to follow?

Oh, goodness, no. No one has ever said anything like that. I've always prided myself on being very clear and logical. You kind of have to be in IT support, you know? You have to explain complicated things to people who might not understand computers very well, so I'm very careful to speak clearly and make sure my thoughts are organized.

I mean, maybe occasionally I'll get a little caught up in the details of a server issue or a ticketing problem, and I might talk a bit fast because I want to make sure I get all the facts out... but it all makes perfect sense. I always make sure people follow what I'm saying. 

I wouldn't want anyone to think I was confused or rambling. That would be terrible for my professional reputation. I'm communicating clearly with you today, right? I hope my answers are making sense and giving you what you need.
Lately, have you found it harder to get yourself started on everyday tasks, even when you want to do them?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've always been very self-motivated, and that hasn't changed at all. I still get up right on time, make my coffee, and get my day started without any issues. 

I mean, keeping a good, reliable routine is so important, right? You have to stay responsible. Even with how exhausting work has been lately—having to monitor everything so closely and document all those tickets—I never let my daily chores or anything around the house slip. I'd be so embarrassed if I let my place get messy or if I couldn't manage my own basic errands. That's just not the kind of person I am. 

I might move a little slower on a Sunday morning, just to catch my breath and have a quiet cup of coffee, but I always get my tasks done. Does that sound like a healthy approach to you? I really do try my best to stay on top of everything and be productive.
Have you ever had a period where your mood was unusually high or irritable?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say so. I've always been a pretty even-keeled person, you know? I try very hard not to let things get to me or fly off the handle. I think it's important to keep a steady, professional attitude, especially at my age. 

I mean, I might get a little frustrated if a user keeps making the same mistake after I've shown them how to fix it, but I never lose my temper. I just take a deep breath and explain it again as politely as I can. And as for being unusually high or, um, overly energetic... no, not really. I like to think I'm just a reliable, steady guy. 

I wouldn't want to be one of those people who is always up and down and making everyone around them uncomfortable. That sounds exhausting for everyone involved. I'm pretty consistent, wouldn't you say? I hope that's the impression I'm giving you.
